newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Tuesday:
* The market's bearish mood is expected to prevail on dearth of compelling, positive news, and any rally after Monday' steep fall will be technical in nature, brokers said.

* "We are looking at a trading range of 2,500 to 2,600 until next week. Perhaps we can see some minor rallies but they will not be sustained because of lack of good news," said Lippo Securities research manager Jidgette Valenzuela.
* On Monday, the Philippine composite index fell sharply, skidding 75.39 points to close at 2,572.43 points.
* The Dow Jones on Monday ended 30.89 points up at 8,062.11. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $1\07 at $30\09.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 28.57 to a U.S. dollar versus 28.51.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 18.0625 percent.
* Philippine banks started buying treasury bills in the secondary market on Monday ahead of an expected slide in interest rates, traders said.
* Metro Pacific Corp plans to retire within the year its $200 million loan from ING Bank, Metro Pacific chairman Manuel Pangilinan said.

* Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Inc (BayanTel), a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp, said it had asked the government to allow a facility under which it could adjust tariffs in line with fluctuations of the Philippine peso.

* Philippine listed banks are likely to post slower growth in the medium-term following the de facto devaluation of the peso, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in a report in which it downgraded the sector to "underweight" from "neutral."

* Smart Communications Co Inc, a unit of Metro Pacific Corp, has formed a joint venture with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to provide internet services in the Philippines, a senior officer of Smart said.
* Metro Pacific reported a 420.4 million peso income excluding other income. Its unaudited consolidated net income was 574 million pesos from 393 million in the year-ago period.
* Newspaper Today said Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito stressed the need to bring back interest rates to their level prior to the peso's depreciation.
* BusinessWorld said Executive Secretary Ruben Torres has urged the Congress to pass the comprehensive tax reform bill rather than make amendments to the bank secrecy law.
* Chronicle reported that based on Department of Finance data, Philippine export growth will remain strong at 23.5 percent this year.
